chapter: Hite tours, postwar L.A. and the Central Avenue scene
title: The Club Alabam's mixed audience
summary: The audience was mixed and visitors from white areas were protected.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Back to the Alabam, the shows were
black and unlike places like New York's Cotton Club, the audience, was it not, predominantly black, however a lot of white folks came down? (inaudible)?

It was neither one nor the other. It was sort of a cosmopolitan feeling around there. There was no animosity against whites or animosity against blacks. If they came down to enjoy themselves, they came down to enjoy themselves. They had to come across town to do it and they were treated well. It was no thing of rip-offs and things just because a white guy came from the other side of town like they have in the ghetto things now. There was no rip-offs or nothing and as a matter of fact, the white guy that came down there was pretty well-protected by the guys that were around there because they knew that if they didn't protect the white guy that came down there, no money came down there.

So, the money was where the white people were and so that was it.
